diagrams.title: Probe L0
diagrams.description: System context: the machine manager is one box. The control plane and humans + mmctl call it; it drives the bare-metal providers, boots and audits the machines, keeps images and diagnostics in S3, and alerts in Slack. Nothing inside is shown yet, so L1 opens it.

diagrams.title: Probe L1
diagrams.description: L0's box opened one level: its boundary services — private gRPC, webapi, provider registry, cluster reconcile, SSH + BMC ops and the boot server — sit in the Machine manager box, while the control plane, humans, providers, machines and S3 stay outside it.

diagrams.title: Probe L1B
diagrams.description: The fleet end of the same system. Bare-metal machines run the machine-agent, which registers and heartbeats into public gRPC inside the manager's box; the River queue uploads diagnostics to S3 and webapi confirms actions in Slack, both outside. The fleet drives these outward relations.

diagrams.title: Probe L2
diagrams.description: The manager's inside: requests land on the River queue, which dispatches provision jobs, audits and diagnostic events; the janitor proposes actions back to webapi, and the queue, private gRPC, public gRPC and reconcile write into Postgres. Every node here is inside the box.
